From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:14:05 -0800
Subject: FW: EdgeML packaging and marketplace passback questions — draft ask for pricing matrix

Team —

Looping you both in to draft a clean counter for GlobalScale. Key constraints from Ellen: first-year net target ~$1.5M; reseller needs a minimum gross margin; they want marketplace credits to be visible on the invoice (so prefer passback rather than off-invoice rebates if possible).

Draft proposal (we'll refine numbers in the matrix):
- Packaging options to present:
  * Option A — Reserved-node SKU (1yr commit): list price at "node-hour" SKU, tiered commit discounts at 25/50/100k node-hrs; overage billed at 1.4x base metered rate.
  * Option B — Metered inference SKU: pay-as-you-go token-based pricing with volume discounts at spend thresholds.
  * Option C — Hybrid: smaller reserved anchor (40% of expected) + metered overage; gives predictability and cheaper marginal cost.

- Commercial levers:
  * Committed discount (applied to list) — reduces list -> net.
  * Channel uplift (pass-through percent to reseller) — applied to net, and shown as line-item credit on marketplace invoice where possible.
  * Off-invoice credits (as backup) — slower for reconciliation; prefer to avoid if procurement insists on invoice visibility.

- Suggested starter numbers (for the matrix):
  * Target gross list for sizing: $2.1M ARR-equivalent (to reach ~$1.5M net after discount / uplift).
  * Committed discount: 22% (1yr) -> net before reseller uplift.
  * Channel uplift to reseller: 8% (passback shown as credit line).
  * If reseller requests higher uplift, propose trade: +3% uplift -> extra 3% reduction in our committed discount (maintain net) or extend commit length to 2 years with same uplift.

I've attached a draft MA plan / matrix (MA_plan_draft.xlsx) with a simple price ladder and a mapping table. Please review and add a column that shows final net-to-GlobalScale and net-to-reseller by structure (list -> discount -> net -> uplift -> reseller-net).

Ask: Ben, can you validate the 'invoice-visible passback' mechanics for AWS Marketplace? Kar, can you run the sensitivity (if uplift goes to 12%) to show impact on our ASP and what commit size would be needed to keep unit economics neutral?

We'll send them a clean matrix and a short bullets doc before the call.

Thanks — t

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the draft matrix. A few clarifications before the call:

> From Tessa: "Channel uplift to reseller: 8% (passback shown as credit line)."

Our reseller is pushing back — they want a 12% uplift as a non-negotiable for their margin model. They indicated they need the uplift reflected as a visible credit on the AWS invoice (not buried as a separate vendor rebate). Can Redwood support a 12% visible passback? If 12% is a stretch, can you show a path where we keep first-year net to Redwood at ~$1.5M by either: (a) increasing total commit, (b) moving to a 2-year commit with a slightly higher discount, or (c) taking some portion as off-invoice credits tied to usage true-up?

Also: we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a short note on data retention for any marketplace SKU — procurement wants that before contract sign. Please cc your security contact or attach the SOC2 link.

Proposed: Let's keep the Wednesday 11/18 10:00 PT call — Ben/Kar on the line if possible. If you can, send the updated table (list -> net -> reseller-net) before the call so procurement can review live.
